title: Equipment Lending System
body:
A staff-managed university lending API
Reliable availability, borrowing and return history
speaker: Hussein Chreif
notes: Introduce all four contributors. Explain the paper/spreadsheet problem and the backend release boundary. Handover: first, the workflow we protect. Source: docs/requirements/requirements.md.

title: Release scope
body:
Student and equipment records
Borrow, return, availability and overdue history
Staff Basic access; public aggregate health
Frontend planned separately in Sprint 5
speaker: Hussein Chreif
notes: Students are borrower records, not login users. Describe one active loan per item and retained history. Do not imply remote HTTPS or browser acceptance. Source: docs/api/contract.md; reports/final-report.md.

title: Application architecture
body:
Controllers: validated DTOs
Services: normalization, rules and transactions
Repositories: PostgreSQL persistence
Flyway: sole schema owner
speaker: Komayl Dbouk
notes: Trace POST /api/loans through the loan package. Shared code is config/errors, not a second application. Explain Hibernate validation versus Flyway migration. Source: docs/design/architecture.md; src/main/java/edu/university/equipmentlending.

title: Database invariants
body:
One active loan per equipment item
Restrictive foreign keys retain history
Due date must follow borrowing date
Lock ordering and transactions protect competing writes
speaker: Komayl Dbouk
notes: The partial unique index is the final concurrency invariant; service checks alone cannot prevent a race. A returned loan remains in history when a new loan is inserted. Source: docs/api/contract.md; src/main/resources/db/migration; ELS-47 TC11. Handover: Mostafa will connect these rules to observable tests.

title: Borrow and return oracles
body:
Compare exact DTO fields with committed SQL
Reject a second return without changing history
Return restores availability
Reborrow creates a new loan; the old row remains
speaker: Mostafa Younes
notes: Explain your student/return work and another member's borrowing rule. ELS-32 preserved red tests before implementation; ELS-47 TC12-TC15 verified return/reborrow. A green HTTP status alone is insufficient. Sources: reports/sprint-2/els-32-test-first-evidence.md; reports/sprint-4/els-47-final-release-acceptance.md.

title: Reviewing AI-assisted work
body:
Weak generated assertions needed independent oracles
A functional query still made 25 database statements
Configuration and SQL logging needed packaged checks
Fault probes and SQL checks exposed hidden gaps
speaker: Mostafa Younes
notes: Distinguish examples: ELS-39 strengthened generated tests; ELS-41 corrected N+1 and SQL-message matching; ELS-46 removed a credential fallback and SQL logging leak. Each speaker should explain one original weakness, correction and test. No unmeasured AI time saving is claimed. Sources: reports/sprint-3/els-39-test-audit.md; reports/sprint-3/els-43-measured-quality-improvement.md; reports/sprint-4/els-46-access-privacy-license-review.md.

title: Measured quality
body:
24-item list: 25 → 1 SQL statements
96% fewer statements; no latency claim
SpotBugs: 9 → 8 warnings
Eight assessed warnings remain
speaker: Hussein Chalhoub
notes: Historical ELS-43 measurements, not fresh measurements of this deck. Explain query projection preserving filters/order/DTOs. Do not compare coverage denominators as if unchanged. Source: reports/sprint-3/els-43-measured-quality-improvement.md.

title: Release acceptance
body:
200 unit/controller + 193 PostgreSQL tests
15 helper checks
227 HTTP requests and three coordinated races
Source-scoped evidence and independent SQL oracles
speaker: Hussein Chalhoub
notes: All counts are historical ELS-47 results at its recorded source; CI assertion count was 3409, local count differed legitimately with race outcomes. This is not proof a team rehearsal occurred. Source: reports/sprint-4/els-47-final-release-acceptance.md; reports/sprint-4/els-47-acceptance-results.json. Handover: we will now show the owned local package.

title: Live demonstration
body:
Health and rejected staff access
Synthetic records, active and returned history
Return → reborrow → overdue → return
Read history, then reset only the owned project
speaker: All four
notes: Follow els-49-demo-runbook.md and els-49-live-workflow.md. Chreif frames health/auth; Mostafa returns; Komayl reborrows and checks overdue; Chalhoub checks history and cleanup. Stop immediately on a failed oracle. Ordinary current Beirut clock; no SQL fixture rewriting. Offline fallback must be labeled historical evidence, not a live pass.

title: Debugging exercise
body:
Symptom: borrowing returns 409
Inspect the public code and request identity
Compare active history and availability
Explain the invariant before changing anything
speaker: All four
notes: Use the scripted unavailable-equipment conflict on the active camera. Expected code EQUIPMENT_UNAVAILABLE; verify unchanged history. Ask another speaker to trace controller, service lock and partial unique index. Do not remove constraints or edit database rows to make the request pass. See runbook Q&A and contract.

title: Safe delivery and limits
body:
Loopback app; database has no host port
Private credentials and synthetic fixtures
Guarded, explicit reset of disposable resources
Remote HTTPS and browser acceptance remain separate
speaker: Hussein Chalhoub
notes: Explain checkpoint target identity and failure-closed reset/seed guards. Neither a Docker run nor these slides prove remote deployment readiness. Distribution closeout belongs to ELS-50. Source: docs/deployment/local-setup.md; docs/deployment/staff-access.md.

title: Discussion
body:
Which independent oracle protects each rule?
What did review correct in AI-assisted output?
What remains outside this release?
speaker: Hussein Chreif
notes: Invite questions. Each member answers one question and explains another feature during the real rehearsal. Record actual answers/corrections in els-49-team-rehearsal.json. Do not mark human rehearsal completed from technical checks. Source: reports/final-report.md; docs/reference-practice-traceability.md.
